NGC 7793 has significantly more molecular gas mass than NGC 1313 and nearly all of that molecular mass is accounted for with identified clouds, suggesting that NGC 1313 has more diffuse molecular gas than NGC 7793.
Both galaxies fall mostly above the virial equilibrium line, suggesting that they are dominated by kinetic energy.
Both the full cluster population and the young clusters of NGC 1313 are further from molecular clouds than those in NGC 7793.
The intercept of NGC 1313 is significantly higher than that of NGC 7793 by more than $3\sigma$, which suggests that NGC 1313 has more kinetic energy in its molecular clouds than NGC 7793.
NGC 1313 also has more clouds near virial equilibrium than NGC 7793, which may be connected to its higher rate of massive cluster formation.
In every case of cell size and $\alpha_\text{vir}$ threshold, the bound clouds are not more correlated with young clusters than the rest of the cloud population in either galaxy.
